text: dsh-notify-plus 是面向 Windows DSH Desktop 的通知插件。它通过 Cordis 行观察由用户发起的会话回合和后台任务，使用当前会话标题，并把回复压缩成简短摘要作为桌面通知；失败回合会显示原因，纯工具调用会显示调用数。旧版主机使用 desktopRuntime，新版通过 Windows PowerShell 5.1 发出原生 toast。适合需要在切换窗口时了解哪个对话或任务已结束的桌面用户。

dsh-notify-plus adds contextual Windows alerts to DSH Desktop. It reports the live conversation title, a short reply summary, turn failures, and completed background jobs. Older hosts use desktopRuntime; newer hosts show native toasts through Windows PowerShell 5.1.
想让 DSH 桌面通知显示刚完成的是哪个会话。
DSH 回合结束时能不能把回复摘要发成 Windows 通知？
I want Windows notifications to identify the DSH conversation and summarize its finished turn.
会话与任务完成通知：插件监听用户发起的 DSH 回合及后台任务结束事件，通知标题使用当前会话名，正文显示回复摘要、失败原因或任务标签；在 Windows 新版主机上由系统 toast 展示。

dsh-notify-plus README · dsh-notify-plus：[English](README.md) | [中文](README.zh.md)

Context-rich native notifications for **DSH Desktop** — both the official
**DeepSeek Harness** shell (`0.2.0-rc.x`) and the earlier `DSH Desktop` shell
(`2.0.x`).

DSH Desktop's built-in notification told you that *a* turn finished. It never
told you *which* conversation, or *what* the turn actually produced — so the
toast was impossible to act on:

dsh-notify-plus README · dsh-notify-plus：| | Built-in | dsh-notify-plus |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Title | `用户回合已完成` / `User Turn Completed` | `重构通知插件` — the live conversation title |
| Body | `一个由你发起的回合已完成。` / `A user-initiated turn has finished.` | `已经修复了通知排序，现在会优先选择最近的助手…` — a distilled one-liner |

dsh-notify-plus README · dsh-notify-plus：On the earlier shell the plugin replaces that built-in row and reuses its
settings namespace, so the existing Desktop toggles keep working and no user
preference is lost. The official 0.2.0 shell removed the row *and* the
notification service a plugin could call, so there the plugin raises the toast
itself. See [How the replacement works](#how-the-replacement-works).

dsh-notify-plus README · What it does：- **Titles every toast with the live conversation title.** The title comes from
  the log-backed session title service, so it follows renames and automatic
  title revisions instead of being a constant.
- **Distils the turn into one actionable line.** For CJK replies the body is
  10–20 characters; for Latin replies it stays inside the Windows toast body
  envelope. Nothing is sent to a model — the distillation is deterministic, so
  it costs no tokens and adds no latency.
- **Keeps failure reasons.** A failed turn reports the actual error instead of a
  generic apology, and a context-exhaustion stop is labelled separately.
- **Carries the job label** on background job notifications, so `pnpm test`
  finishing is distinguishable from several other jobs finishing at once.
- **Never fires for internal fan-out.** Delegated subagent sessions and turns
  that no user message started are ignored, exactly like the built-in row.

dsh-notify-plus README · Requirements：| | |
| --- | --- |
| DSH Desktop | the official **DeepSeek Harness** shell — verified against `0.2.0-rc.2` — and the earlier `DSH Desktop` shell — verified against `2.0.3` |
| Harness | `@deepseek-ai/dsh 0.2.0-rc.x`, and `0.1.1-rc.x` on the earlier shell |
| Windows | 10 or 11. The toast path uses Windows PowerShell 5.1 and the installed DSH Desktop AUMID |
| Node | `>=22.19.0` (only for development and tests) |

dsh-notify-plus README · Requirements：The plugin depends on one harness-provided module, `@deepseek-ai/schemastery`,
which DSH already mounts. You do not need to install it yourself.

dsh-notify-plus README · From the DSH Desktop Market：Search for `dsh-notify-plus` in the Desktop plugin market and install it. The
market writes the package into the active profile's `dsh.profile.bundles`, which
is all this plugin needs.

dsh-notify-plus README · From the command line：```powershell
dsh plugin --profile <your-profile> add dsh-notify-plus
```

`dsh plugin` is a pnpm forwarder: it installs the package into the profile and
reconciles `dsh.profile.bundles` against the installed state. A package that
declares `dsh.bundle.patch` — this one does — joins the layer stack
automatically.

dsh-notify-plus README · From a local checkout：```powershell
git clone https://github.com/hoyin-law/dsh-notify-plus.git
dsh plugin --profile <your-profile> add C:\path\to\dsh-notify-plus
```

Then restart DSH Desktop. Confirm the row is live before assuming anything:

```powershell
dsh --profile <your-profile> dump-config | Select-String "dsh-notify-plus"
```

dsh-notify-plus README · How the replacement works：Both rows are Cordis plugins. Rather than racing the built-in observer (which
would raise two toasts per turn), this plugin ships a bundle patch that disables
the built-in row and inserts its own:

```yaml
- id: desktop-notifications
  disabled: true

- insert:

On the official 0.2.0 shell there is no `desktop-notifications` row to disable,
and the DSH loader reports an id-targeted patch that matches nothing as a
warning, so the first entry is inert there and the plugin is purely additive.

dsh-notify-plus README · Raising the toast：The notification surface changed underneath this plugin, and the change is the
reason 0.2.0 needs its own path:

dsh-notify-plus README · Raising the toast：| | earlier `DSH Desktop` 2.0.x | official `DeepSeek Harness` 0.2.0 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Host process | Cordis host boots inside the Electron main process | host boots as a **separate Node child process** (`spawn(node, [...dsh-desktop-host/lib/index.js])`) |
| Plugin surface | `desktopRuntime.notifyAttention({ title, body })` | **none** — `desktopRuntime` has zero occurrences in the shipped app |
| Built-in row | `desktop-notifications` with hard-coded copy | removed entirely; `dsh-desktop-notifications` has zero occurrences |
| Host → shell IPC | in-process | open, but a closed protocol: only `ready`, `platform-session`, `fatal`, `shutdown-complete`, `update-tasks`, and `quit-inspection` are accepted, and an unknown message makes the shell kill the host |

dsh-notify-plus README · Raising the toast：So the plugin keeps `desktopRuntime` as an **optional** injection — where it
exists, the original call is used unchanged — and otherwise raises a native
Windows toast itself:

dsh-notify-plus README · Raising the toast：1. the notification is encoded as base64 UTF-8 JSON, so quotes, newlines, and
   CJK never touch a command line where PowerShell's `-File` parsing could
   mangle them;
2. Windows PowerShell **5.1** (not `pwsh`, which dropped the WinRT type
   projection) decodes it and shows a `ToastText02` through
   `CreateToastNotifier("com.deepseek.dsh")` — the AUMID of the installed
   Start Menu shortcut, which is what makes the toast read as DeepSeek Harness
   and land in the Action Center;
3. before showing, the script checks whether `DeepSeek Harness.exe` owns the
   foreground window and stays silent if it does, matching the old host's
   focus suppression. The check **fails open**: an unreadable foreground window
   raises the toast rather than swallowing it.

dsh-notify-plus README · Raising the toast：The sink also degrades instead of throwing: if PowerShell cannot be spawned the
plugin keeps running, logs once, and stops trying, so a broken notification path
can never disturb the turn that produced it.

dsh-notify-plus README · Why the bundle declares no DSH peer dependencies：DSH 0.2.0 refuses to load any plugin whose `peerDependencies` on
`@deepseek-ai/dsh*` do not satisfy the running runtime — a `^0.1.0-rc.x` range
fails against `0.2.0-rc.2`, and the row is disabled before it is imported. This
plugin consumes only services (`sessions`, `jobs`, `settings`, `sessionTitle`,
`desktopRuntime`) and imports nothing from the harness except `schemastery`,
which is not covered by that check. Staying off the DSH peer surface is
therefore deliberate: it is what lets one build load on both hosts.
section: Why the bundle declares no DSH peer dependencies

dsh-notify-plus README · Settings：On the official 0.2.0 shell the plugin exports a Cordis `Config`, so every field
appears in **Settings** and is persisted into the active profile's
`cordis.patch.yml`:

dsh-notify-plus README · Settings：| Key | Default | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled` | `true` | Master switch for every notification |
| `notifyOnTurnCompletion` | `true` | A conversation turn finished |
| `notifyOnTurnFailure` | `true` | A conversation turn failed or ran out of context |
| `notifyOnJobCompletion` | `true` | A background job finished |
| `notifyOnJobFailure` | `true` | A background job failed |
| `locale` | `auto` | `auto` follows the host locale; `zh` or `en` force one |
| `appId` | `com.deepseek.dsh` | AUMID the toast is attributed to |
| `suppressWhenFocused` | `true` | Stay silent while DSH Desktop owns the foreground |
| `focusProcess` | `DeepSeek Harness` | Process name that counts as focused |

dsh-notify-plus README · Settings：The same values can be set by hand in the profile:

```yaml
- id: dsh-notify-plus
  config:
    notifyOnJobCompletion: false
    locale: zh

On the earlier 2.0.x shell the plugin additionally registers the
`dsh-desktop-notifications` namespace with the same five switches, so
**Settings → Notifications** keeps controlling it exactly as before. That
namespace wins over the row config, and it is only registered where the old
scope API still exists.

dsh-notify-plus README · Settings：Nothing fires for work you are already watching: the toast script stays silent
while the DSH Desktop window owns the foreground.

dsh-notify-plus README · A known upstream caveat：This applies to the earlier 2.0.x shell, which still ships the
`profile-preferences` record.

dsh-notify-plus README · A known upstream caveat：On those releases, edits made in **Settings → Notifications** may revert on the
next launch. The desktop keeps a private copy of `mode`, `openBrowser`,
`networkExposure`, and `notifications` under
`<userData>/profile-preferences/<profileHash>/state.json` and mirrors it back
into `settings.yaml` at startup, while the settings page only writes
`settings.yaml`. This plugin reads whatever the document says, so it inherits the
revert exactly as the built-in row does.

dsh-notify-plus README · A known upstream caveat：Tracked upstream as
[issue #947](https://github.com/anywhere-labs/deepseek-harness-desktop/issues/947).
DSH Desktop 2.0.3 does not contain that mechanism and is unaffected; the report
is against 2.0.9, and the mirroring code first appears in a later release than
2.0.3.

dsh-notify-plus README · A known upstream caveat：This is deliberately **not** worked around here. That record is another
component's private source of truth: writing it from a plugin would add a second
writer to a single-document record that also holds the user's browser and
network-exposure choices.

dsh-notify-plus README · Compatibility：This plugin reads harness internals that are not a stable public contract:
`sessions.on("session/event")`, `ctx.get("sessionTitle")`, the background-job
settlement stream (`jobs.onJobDone` on 0.1.x, `jobs.events.subscribe` on 0.2.0),
and the notification surface (`desktopRuntime.notifyAttention` on 0.1.x; a
self-contained Windows toast on 0.2.0). Each of those is driven behind a
feature check and covered by tests against the verified shapes.

dsh-notify-plus README · Compatibility：Because the notification surface is now the plugin's own, a host that provides
nothing still loads: the session observers run, the sink reports why it stayed
silent, and one broken notification never disturbs the turn that produced it.
A release that changes the session or job shapes will stop producing that kind
of notification; please open an issue with your DSH Desktop version.

dsh-notify-plus README · DSH STORE status：This plugin is **not listed in [DSH STORE](https://dsh.store/)**. The store's
automated policy declines any bundle patch that disables a shipped entry, and
disabling one is exactly what makes this plugin work: without it, the built-in
`desktop-notifications` row keeps raising its own toast, and the two plugins
cannot coexist at all — both register the `dsh-desktop-notifications` settings
namespace, and `settings.register()` throws on a duplicate, so the second one
fails its row.

dsh-notify-plus README · DSH STORE status：- The row this plugin disables belongs to `dsh-plugin-desktop` (the DSH Desktop
  launcher), not to a `@deepseek-ai/*` package. No official harness package,
  entry ID, or namespace is modified.
- The replacement is exact: the plugin re-registers the same settings namespace
  with the same five keys, so the Desktop switches keep working and no user
  preference is lost.
- Install and start were verified end to end on DSH Desktop 2.0.3; see
  [Verifying a live install](#verifying-a-live-install).

dsh-notify-plus README · DSH STORE status：Install it from the repository instead:

```powershell
dsh plugin --profile <your-profile> add https://github.com/hoyin-law/dsh-notify-plus
```

A future release may make the disable an explicit opt-in in the user's own
profile layer, which would let the bundle patch become purely additive. That
needs the plugin to fall back to its own settings namespace when the built-in
row is still present, so it is a behaviour change rather than a packaging tweak.

dsh-notify-plus README · Upstream status：The capability this plugin adds is being implemented natively. Upstream `master`
still ships the hard-coded copy, but
[PR #969](https://github.com/anywhere-labs/deepseek-harness-desktop/pull/969)
adds session titles as notification headings plus a final-answer preview, and
[issue #951](https://github.com/anywhere-labs/deepseek-harness-desktop/issues/951)
asks for host-level governance of third-party plugin notifications.
[`docs/upstream-request.md`](docs/upstream-request.md) records the duplicate
check that stopped us filing a new request, the relevant threads, and what is
worth contributing to them.

dsh-notify-plus README · Upstream status：If that work lands in a DSH Desktop release, this plugin should be retired
rather than kept alive by disabling an official row that is already correct.

dsh-notify-plus README · Declared compatibility：`package.json` carries a per-release declaration under
`dsh.compatibility.dshReleases`. Every entry is either runtime-verified or
interface-verified against the published package — never assumed:

dsh-notify-plus README · Declared compatibility：| DSH release | Basis |
| --- | --- |
| `0.2.0-rc.2` | runtime-verified: installed into a live profile on the official **DeepSeek Harness** shell and observed raising a correctly-shaped toast through the AUMID path |
| `0.1.1-rc.2` | runtime-verified: installed into a live `web` profile on DSH Desktop 2.0.3 and observed raising correctly-shaped toasts |
| `0.1.5-alpha.2` | interface-verified: every consumed surface has an identical signature and payload shape |
| `0.1.5-rc.1` | interface-verified: same |
| `0.1.5-rc.2` | interface-verified: same |

dsh-notify-plus README · Declared compatibility："Interface-verified" means the consumed surfaces — `sessions.on("session/event")`
with the `turn/start`, `turn/end`, `assistant/message`, and `user/message`
payloads; `sessionTitle.get(session)`; the job settlement stream; and
`settings.register(ns, schema, options)` — were diffed against each release's
published types and sources and found unchanged. It is a source-level claim, not
a runtime acceptance, and it is labelled as such.

dsh-notify-plus README · Declared compatibility：`0.2.0-rc.2` additionally changed three of those surfaces, all of which are
handled here: `jobs.onJobDone(snapshot)` became
`jobs.events.subscribe({ owners }, listener)` delivering a `settled` event whose
`job` carries `status` and `label`; the namespace-scope settings API was
replaced by a `Config`-derived form model, so the plugin exports `Config` and
keeps the legacy namespace only as a bridge; and the native notification service
disappeared with the in-process host.

dsh-notify-plus README · Declared compatibility：Only `win32` and the DSH Desktop host are declared. The observation layer is
platform-neutral, but the notification path is Windows-only, so nothing else has
been run.

dsh-notify-plus README · Development：```powershell
npm install            # only needed for the harness-provided schemastery peer
npm test               # 106 assertions across 7 suites, no harness required
npm run verify:layering   # composes the real patch layers via the dsh CLI
```

dsh-notify-plus README · Development：The test suite covers the pure layers — summarisation, copy, session
projections, the turn/job state machine, the settings bridge, and the
notification sinks — with hand-built fixtures and an injected spawn stub, so the
behavioural contract is checked without launching Electron or raising a toast.

dsh-notify-plus README · Development：`.volatile()` is feature-detected: the dev schemastery (3.18.2) predates it, so
the suite exercises the fallback path and skips the volatility assertion; the
0.2.0 Desktop ships 3.18.4 and the 0.1.x Desktop ships 3.18.1.

dsh-notify-plus README · Development：`verify:layering` is the one check that needs DSH Desktop installed. It builds a
throwaway `DSH_HOME`, stands in for the launcher-owned layer, and asks the real
`dsh --dump-config` to compose the tree, asserting that the built-in row ends up
`disabled: true`, that this plugin's row follows it, and that a host without the
built-in row still exits `0` with only a warning. Point it elsewhere if your
installation is not in the default location:

dsh-notify-plus README · Development：```powershell
node scripts/verify-layering.mjs --app "D:\Apps\DSH Desktop\DSH Desktop.exe"
```

```
lib/
  index.js       Cordis wiring: config, settings bridge, jobs, sessions
  notify.js      notification sinks: host runtime, Windows toast, null
  turn.js        session event -> notification payload state machine

dsh-notify-plus README · Verifying a live install：Neither notification path leaves an application log line — Electron's
`Notification` did not, and a PowerShell toast does not — so the only reliable
check is the shell's own toast history:

```powershell
node tools/read-windows-toasts.mjs --limit 10
```

dsh-notify-plus README · Verifying a live install：Both paths also stay silent while the DSH Desktop window owns the foreground, so
a focused test can look like a no-op. To observe a toast without waiting for a
real turn to finish, exercise the sink directly; this raises one regardless of
focus and proves the whole chain — PowerShell resolution, payload encoding,
spawn, script, AUMID:

dsh-notify-plus README · Verifying a live install：```powershell
node --input-type=module -e "import('file:///C:/path/to/dsh-notify-plus/lib/notify.js').then(async ({createToastSink}) => { const s = createToastSink({ readConfig: () => ({ enabled: true, locale: 'zh', appId: 'com.deepseek.dsh', focusProcess: '', suppressWhenFocused: false }) }); s.notifyAttention({ title: 'dsh-notify-plus', body: 'sink check' }); })"
```

A working replacement looks like this, with the cutover exactly at the restart:

dsh-notify-plus README · Verifying a live install：```
2026/9/14 04:33:35  title="重构通知插件"   body="已经修复了通知排序逻辑，现在会优先…"
2026/9/14 04:23:24  title="用户回合已完成"  body="一个由你发起的回合已完成。"
```

One row per turn, the title is a real conversation name, the body is a truncated
distillation rather than a fixed sentence, and the hard-coded row stops appearing
at the restart rather than alongside the new one — which is what proves the
built-in observer was disabled instead of merely joined.
